title: Richard Jupp on leaving Elbow and his recovery from addiction

evidence_packet.title: Richard Jupp on leaving Elbow and his recovery from addiction
evidence_packet.lead: Elbow's drummer Richard Jupp had everything...
evidence_packet.summary: Elbow's drummer Richard Jupp had everything... but still knew he was heading in the wrong direction
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Richard Jupp spent nearly 30 years of his life in Elbow From gigging in the pubs of Bury and Manchester to sell-out tours and winning international accolades, the drummer seemed to have everything a musician could ever want But underneath the surface the "myth of rock'n'roll" was not what it seemed "From the outside, I had everything you're supposed to want," he explaned "I was travelling the world, making records and living a life I'd dreamed about since I was a kid. We were at an extraordinary point in the band's career "But I asked myself 'What is any of that worth if I'm heading in a direction that was no longer working for me'?"

title: Manchester priest's sermon lands cameo role in Oasis documentary

evidence_packet.title: Manchester priest's sermon lands cameo role in Oasis documentary
evidence_packet.lead: Father Luke Bradbury says he was stunned to be invited to attend the Oasis film's London premiere
evidence_packet.summary: Father Luke Bradbury says he was stunned to be invited to attend the Oasis film's London premiere
evidence_packet.evidence_text: A Burnage priest whose sermon on forgiveness featured in the new Oasis documentary has described the "bizarre" experience of walking the red carpet at its London premiere Father Luke Bradbury, from St Bernard's Church, briefly appears in the film Don't Look Back In Anger, which charts the band's 2025 reunion tour after years of acrimony between siblings Liam and Noel Gallagher The documentary crew wanted to film at the church close to where the brothers appeared in a nativity play as boys, in a nod to their devout Irish Catholic mother Peggy "I was asked if they could film and we had no problem," said Father Bradbury He added: "They were filming during Mass and the Gospel that day was about the apostle Peter asking how often should he forgive his brother and Jesus says 'Seventy times seven' "I happened to make the connection between this and Noel and Liam and it ended up in the documentary near the end of the film."

title: Heidi 'The Hit Girl', 8, dreaming of darts glory in Oldham

evidence_packet.title: Heidi 'The Hit Girl', 8, dreaming of darts glory in Oldham
evidence_packet.lead: Eight-year-old Heidi wants to inspire more girls to play with her at a booming darts academy in Oldham
evidence_packet.summary: Eight-year-old Heidi wants to inspire more girls to play with her at a booming darts academy in Oldham
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Heidi "The Hit Girl" may throw darts bearing Luke Littler's name, but the eight-year-old is dreaming of sporting glory in her own right She also hopes to inspire more girls to take to the oche and show that darts can be for everyone Heidi is one of about 200 young players who attend Boundary Park Darts Academy in Oldham, Greater Manchester, each week. It is believed to be one of the largest youth darts clubs in the UK "There's not a lot of girls out there that play darts," she said. "But I thought I'd give it a shot to inspire some others to start playing because it's really fun." When she's not competing at Boundary Park, Heidi practises at home in her parents' kitchen "I really want to become a professional darts player," she told BBC Radio Manchester. "I want to be on telly so everyone can see that kids my age can get really good at something."

Layers of linen were carefully peeled away from the 2,700-year-old remains of the woman named Asru when she was first taken out of her wooden coffin and put on public display in Manchester in 1825. Centuries later, her remains have been placed in storage in a decision that "aligns most closely with what we understand about her own wishes", a Manchester Museum spokesman said. "Elite Egyptians of her time expected that their mummified bodies would remain wrapped in their coffins, invisible to the living," he added. Image source, Manchester Museum Image caption, The wooden coffin was on display in the Egypt and Sudan collections Asru's mummified body had been on display in the Oxford Road museum's Egypt and Sudan Gallery before it was moved into storage earlier this month. She was mummified in a series of rituals used by ancient Egyptians to preserve the body after death in preparation for the afterlife. Her remains and coffins were dug up in modern Luxor, the site of the ancient city of Thebes, before they ended up in the ownership of Manchester traders William and Robert Garnett in the early 1800s. The body was donated to the Manchester Natural History Society in 1825 and placed on display for the next two centuries. title: Wigan Council renames town square in honour of Sir Billy Boston

evidence_packet.title: Wigan Council renames town square in honour of Sir Billy Boston
evidence_packet.lead: Sir Billy Boston was "a pioneer" and "an inspiration" and his legacy will continue, Wigan Council says
evidence_packet.summary: Sir Billy Boston was "a pioneer" and "an inspiration" and his legacy will continue, Wigan Council says
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Rugby League star Sir Billy Boston is to be further honoured in his adopted hometown Wigan, with the renaming of the town's square where his statue is situated Sir Billy, who was Rugby league's first knight, died last month, aged 92. His funeral took place at Wigan Warriors' Brick Community Stadium on Thursday Believe Square will now be called Sir Billy Boston Square "to ensure his legacy continues" in the heart of the town, Wigan Council has announced In March, a civic service was held to mark a new plaque being added to his statue, following his knighthood in 2025 Born in Cardiff in 1934, Sir Billy grew up playing rugby union but faced prejudice because of his ethnicity and was overlooked by his home club He came to the attention of rugby league scouts while on national service in the north of England, signing for Wigan in 1953 as a 19-year-old

The stretch of road directly connects Manchester and Sheffield, but it is littered with problems View 5 Images An aerial view of the A57 Snake Pass making its way through the Peak District an News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 16:19, 12 Sep 2026 Updated 16:19, 12 Sep 2026 When choosing to drive between Manchester and Sheffield, on paper, it should be a picturesque journey The Snake Pass offers stunning views of the Peak District National Park and a smattering of quaint village stop-offs. But the reality can be very different Many commuters know the route can be as treacherous as its serpentine name suggests, with steep slopes and sharp corners Funnily enough it was actually named after the Snake Inn, rather than its snake-like appearance. The pub was later renamed the Snake Pass Inn, after the Snake Pass The road, also known as the A57, is notoriously littered with problems. It is regularly shut in winter when heavy rain or icy weather makes the route hazardous

Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 12:11, 12 Sep Manchester Museum has removed the remains of an Egyptian mummy after more than 200 years on display. The decision was made by curators at the museum as part of efforts to respect "the wishes of the dead" Last year, the Manchester Museum asked visitors whether they thought they should remove the body of Asru, a woman who lived in Thebes some 2,700 years ago, from the exhibition he body of Asru has been on display at the museum since she was unwrapped there in 1825. A spokesperson for the Museum has now said, having considered the year-long consultation: “The decision to remove Asru from display aligns most closely with what we understand about her own w “Elite Egyptians of her time expected that their mummified bodies would remain wrapped in their coffins, invisible to the living “Before making this change, we consulted with Egyptian colleagues, members of the Egyptian diaspora and visitors to the Museum, helping us to understand people’s feelings about care for mummified people.”

The stretch of road directly connects Manchester and Sheffield, but it is littered with problems View 5 Images An aerial view of the A57 Snake Pass making its way through the Peak District an News George Lythgoe Local De
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Snake Pass What is happening with the notorious Snake Pass? The stretch of road directly connects Manchester and Sheffield, but it is littered with problems View 5 Images An aerial view of the A57 Snake Pass making its way through the Peak District an News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 16:19, 12 Sep 2026 Updated 16:19, 12 Sep 2026 When choosing to drive between Manchester and Sheffield, on paper, it should be a picturesque journey The Snake Pass offers stunning views of the Peak District National Park and a smattering of quaint village stop-offs. But the reality can be very different Many commuters know the route can be as treacherous as its serpentine name suggests, with steep slopes and sharp corners Funnily enough it was actually named after the Snake Inn, rather than its snake-like appearance. The pub was later renamed the Snake Pass Inn, after the Snake Pass The road, also known as the A57, is notoriously littered with problems. It is regularly shut in winter when heavy rain or icy weather makes the route hazardous

Ethan Mason, who is originally from Nantwich in Cheshire, used social media to blackmail children into sendin The 22-year-old appeared at Chester Crown Court on Wednesday 9 September, where he was sentenced to four years in prison. Mason, now of Hyacinth Court, Newcastle-under-Lyme, was also ordered to sign the sex offenders register indefinitely and handed indefinite restraining orders He had earlier pleaded guilty to two counts of making indecent images of children, three counts of engaging in sexual communications with a child, distribution of indecent images if children, causing a child to engage in sexual activity and sending a photograph of genitals to cau Cheshire Police said the investigation began in February 2023 when the mum of a girl in Manchester contacted police reporting that her 12-year-old daughter had been engaging with a man on Snapchat who was using the username ‘CHESHIREPOLICE1’ During the conversations the user had threatened the victim, stating that if she didn’t send him naked images of herself, then he would come to her house. evidence_packet.title: Manchester Museum removes Egyptian mummy from display out of 'respect for the dead'
evidence_packet.lead: Manchester Museum Manchester Museum removes Egyptian mummy from display out of 'respect for the dead' The mummified remains of Asru have been on display at the museum for more than 200 years.
evidence_packet.summary: Manchester Museum Manchester Museum removes Egyptian mummy from display out of 'respect for the dead' The mummified remains of Asru have been on display at the museum for more than 200 years. Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 12:11, 12 Sep Manchester Museum has removed
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Museum Manchester Museum removes Egyptian mummy from display out of 'respect for the dead' The mummified remains of Asru have been on display at the museum for more than 200 years. Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 12:11, 12 Sep Manchester Museum has removed the remains of an Egyptian mummy after more than 200 years on display. The decision was made by curators at the museum as part of efforts to respect "the wishes of the dead" Last year, the Manchester Museum asked visitors whether they thought they should remove the body of Asru, a woman who lived in Thebes some 2,700 years ago, from the exhibition he body of Asru has been on display at the museum since she was unwrapped there in 1825. A spokesperson for the Museum has now said, having considered the year-long consultation: “The decision to remove Asru from display aligns most closely with what we understand about her own w “Elite Egyptians of her time expected that their mummified bodies would remain wrapped in their coffins, invisible to the living “Before making this change, we consulted with Egyptian colleagues, members of the Egyptian diaspora and visitors to the Museum, helping us to understand people’s feelings about care for mummified people.”

evidence_packet.summary: Snake Pass What is happening with the notorious Snake Pass? The stretch of road directly connects Manchester and Sheffield, but it is littered with problems View 5 Images An aerial view of the A57 Snake Pass making its way through the Peak District an News George Lythgoe Local De
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Snake Pass What is happening with the notorious Snake Pass? The stretch of road directly connects Manchester and Sheffield, but it is littered with problems View 5 Images An aerial view of the A57 Snake Pass making its way through the Peak District an News George Lythgoe Local Democracy Reporter 16:19, 12 Sep 2026 Updated 16:19, 12 Sep 2026 When choosing to drive between Manchester and Sheffield, on paper, it should be a picturesque journey The Snake Pass offers stunning views of the Peak District National Park and a smattering of quaint village stop-offs. But the reality can be very different Many commuters know the route can be as treacherous as its serpentine name suggests, with steep slopes and sharp corners Funnily enough it was actually named after the Snake Inn, rather than its snake-like appearance. The pub was later renamed the Snake Pass Inn, after the Snake Pass The road, also known as the A57, is notoriously littered with problems. It is regularly shut in winter when heavy rain or icy weather makes the route hazardous

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Courts Manchester mum horrified after pervert targeted daughter, 12, on Snapchat calling himself 'Cheshire Police' Ethan Mason, 22, was found to have targeted several girls from Manchester and Lancashire News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 15:08, 12 S A horrified mum in Manchester went to the police after discovering her 12-year-old daughter had been engaging with a pervert on Snapchat using the name ‘CHESHIREPOLICE1’. Ethan Mason, who is originally from Nantwich in Cheshire, used social media to blackmail children into sendin The 22-year-old appeared at Chester Crown Court on Wednesday 9 September, where he was sentenced to four years in prison. Mason, now of Hyacinth Court, Newcastle-under-Lyme, was also ordered to sign the sex offenders register indefinitely and handed indefinite restraining orders He had earlier pleaded guilty to two counts of making indecent images of children, three counts of engaging in sexual communications with a child, distribution of indecent images if children, causing a child to engage in sexual activity and sending a photograph of genitals to cau Cheshire Police said the investigation began in February 2023 when the mum of a girl in Manchester contacted police reporting that her 12-year-old daughter had been engaging with a man on Snapchat who was using the username ‘CHESHIREPOLICE1’ During the conversations the user had threatened the victim, stating that if she didn’t send him naked images of herself, then he would come to her house. Fearing for what he may do, the victim sent a number of images and videos of herself to the offender

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Manchester Museum Manchester Museum removes Egyptian mummy from display out of 'respect for the dead' The mummified remains of Asru have been on display at the museum for more than 200 years. Comments News Lee Grimsditch Features Writer 12:11, 12 Sep Manchester Museum has removed the remains of an Egyptian mummy after more than 200 years on display. The decision was made by curators at the museum as part of efforts to respect "the wishes of the dead" Last year, the Manchester Museum asked visitors whether they thought they should remove the body of Asru, a woman who lived in Thebes some 2,700 years ago, from the exhibition he body of Asru has been on display at the museum since she was unwrapped there in 1825. A spokesperson for the Museum has now said, having considered the year-long consultation: “The decision to remove Asru from display aligns most closely with what we understand about her own w “Elite Egyptians of her time expected that their mummified bodies would remain wrapped in their coffins, invisible to the living “Before making this change, we consulted with Egyptian colleagues, members of the Egyptian diaspora and visitors to the Museum, helping us to understand people’s feelings about care for mummified people.”

Comments News Declan Carey Local Democracy Reporter 08:14, 12 Sep 2026 View Image Greater Manch There has been a massive increase in the amount of drugs being seized by Greater Manchester Police (GMP), new figures show In March 2026 there were a total of 2,835kg of drugs recovered by police, up by more than 180 per cent from 1000kg in March 2025 The figures were shared in a Greater Manchester Combined Authority (GMCA) report about GMP’s efforts at tackling serious and organised crime around the region A GMP spokesperson said: “Seizures are up in line with an increase in stop searches, arrests, and line closures, and we are recovering more of all types of drugs “This reflects our commitment to tackle the distribution, production, preparation and exportation of controlled drugs within our communities, and pursue those involved relentlessly.”

Credit: ITV News Reform UK and Labour have gone through to the second round of voting in the Greater Manchester Mayoral by-ele Neither Labour's Bev Craig or Reform UK's Sian Astley managed to secure a majority, meaning voters second choice ballots will now be counted to decide an overall winner Five candidates have now been eliminated from the contest to become Greater Manchester mayor – Geraldine Coggins (Green), Phil Eckersley (Conservative), Marcus Farmer (Independent), Richard Kilpatrick (Liberal Democrats) and Marlon West (Restore Britain) The by-election is using a voting system called supplementary vote (SV), which sees voters mark their ballot papers with a first and second choice, and if any candidate wins more than 50% of the first-choice votes, they are declared the winner That has not happened in Greater Manchester, so the top two candidates, Labour’s Bev Craig and Reform UK candidate Sian Astley, move to a second round ITV Granada Reports' Political Correspondent Lise McNally sent the latest from the Co-op Live as counting for the second round got underway

Skip to content 12.09.2026 • , and Jack Dulhanty , and Alec Herron , and Lucy McLaughlin | The private school money couldn’t save: why did Alderley Edge School for Girls close? Illustration by Jake Greenhalgh ‘If it’s just a million pound, I can write a cheque to keep it going’ The parents at Alderley Edge School for Girls keep comparing their lives to a Netflix drama. “It’s like a Netflix Drama,” says Mike Ward, whose daughter started at the school in January. Or, “it could be a Netflix special,” Adam Gough – whose daughter until recently attended the school’s nursery – tells me. So what would be the opening scene? Would it be when, in one of the first meetings after the school announced its imminent closure, one parent stood up and matter-of-factly said: “if it’s just a million pound, I can write a cheque to keep it going”? Or maybe this. Gough is sitting front row of the nursery obstacle race when his phone goes off with a bing . It’s sports day here at AESG — a fee-paying institution that until last June sat on five-and-a-half acres in the leafiest bit of Cheshire, charged over £6k per pupil per term, and boasted results in the top 3% in the country. It’s the 19th of June, a clear day. About 60 or 70 sets of parents are gathered in the sports field. The email arrives at 9am on the dot. evidence_packet.summary: Fiona Ledden has announced that she will begin a journey to retirement next year following 8 years as the chief legal advisor for Manchester City Council and Salford City Council
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Fiona Ledden has announced that she will begin a journey to retirement next year following 8 years as the chief legal advisor for Manchester City Council and Salford City Council Fiona has enjoyed a distinguished career in local government law and public service, first qualifying as a solicitor in 1985 She has held range of senior leadership positions across local government, including roles at Stoke-on-Trent City Council, the London Borough of Brent, the Greater London Authority and the London Borough of Sutton Fiona joined Manchester City Council as City Solicitor in 2018, taking up a role that shares services with Salford City Council – an agreement that has been in place since 2012 to share resources and reduces costs across the two city councils A respected member of the legal services profession, Fiona served as President of the Manchester Law Society in 2025, representing and supporting the legal community across the region Fiona will stand down as City Solicitor in May 2027. The process to find her replacement is now underway

A total of 53 schools across Manchester achieved a prestigious Green Flag Award during the 2025/26 academic year - a 26% increase on last year and marking the The achievement reflects the dedication and enthusiasm of pupils, teachers and wider school communities who have worked together to take positive environmental action while helping to build a more sustainable city Local schools across Manchester came together at Wythenshawe Park in July this year to celebrate their success and raise awareness as they joined in on a packed day of nature-based activities The impact of Manchester's Eco-Schools network this year has been significant with More than half of Manchester's Green Flag schools achieved the award with distinction, almost doubling the proportion from the previous year

Officers spoke to those at the encampment, who said they intended to leave by Saturday 8th August As the site had not been vacated, the Council returned with support from Greater Manchester Police on Tuesday 11th August. A formal direction was served under Section 77 of the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, requiring those at the encampment to leave and remove their The Council also provided information about authorised sites in Greater Manchester, along with advice about health, wellbeing and reporting hate crime After the direction was not followed, the Council began court proceedings. evidence_packet.evidence_text: Thirteen local artists, schools, charities and community groups have been chosen to bring their ideas to life during Oldham’s year as Greater Manchester Town of Culture From theatre, film and music to a new mural and giant fuzzy felt artwork, the projects cover a wide range of art forms and celebrate Oldham’s people, places and stories Oldham secured the Town of Culture title with its programme, Rising Up . evidence_packet.evidence_text: The Council's Community Safety Service received a Closure Order for a house following reports of persistent anti-social behaviour and criminal activity The order, which is in place for three months, was granted by magistrates under the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014. The order makes it an offence for anyone, including the occupants, from entering the property while it is in force and restricts access only to Reports linked to the address included disorderly and intimidating behaviour, suspected drug-related activity and the order aims to provide respite to residents and protect them from disruption Closure Orders can be obtained by councils and police where a property is linked to serious nuisance, disorder or criminal activity The order will remain in place for three months initially. evidence_packet.evidence_text: A new ‘trainer flat’ which gives cared for young people a taste of what it is like to live independently has been opened by Rochdale Borough Council Living alone for the first time can be a daunting experience, but it can be an even greater challenge for those who have grown up in care as some may only have a limited support network that they can rely on This can make adjusting to new responsibilities such as paying utility bills, managing a tenancy agreement, budgeting and keeping on top of household chores harder However, through the help of the local authority’s trainer flat scheme, of which there are now 14 across the borough, cared for young people aged 17 and over are being offered the perfect stepping stone to safely prepare for life on their own Fully furnished and equipped with everyday household goods, these flats provide young people with the time and support they need to develop the knowledge, skills and confidence to successfully transition into adulthood This support is offered without the financial pressures normally associated with setting up a home, with the young people not required to contribute towards gas, electricity, water and other property-related utility costs until they turn 18

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Experience the raw, unfiltered power of Balkan folklore in a new immersive show from the world’s most famous performance artist Balkan Erotic Epic is a bold new performance work created by the iconic artist Marina Abramović . Regarded as the world’s most influential performance artist, Abramović’s transformative work has reached millions of people – from opening the Pyramid Stage at Glastonbury Festival t A four-hour ritual where ancient myth meets performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic explores the eroticism, spirituality and traditions of Abramović’s homeland through 13 visceral scenes Brought to life by a cast of over 70 performers, dancers, musicians and singers, the experience unfolds across Aviva Studios. Audiences are free to choose their own path – with pop-up encounters punctuating the action, bringing bodies together in dance, song and ritual Watch Fertility Rite , a fevered ritual where bodies writhe against the ground in a desperate call for fertility. Witness Massaging the Breast where women gesticulate over graves to awaken the earth. In Scaring the Gods , women bare themselves to the sky to banish storms. Listen Unafraid to push the boundaries of eroticism and performance art, Balkan Erotic Epic asks its audience a timeless question: What are our bodies truly for?

evidence_packet.evidence_text: Works will soon begin to ensure the preservation and protection of one of Manchester city centre’s most recognised landmarks For nearly four decades, the iconic Chinatown archway has stood as the gateway to the city’s famous Chinatown. The Grade II-listed structure was a gift from Beijing to the people of Manchester, assembled by Chinese artisans between 1986-87 Works will begin on a two-year project of repair and restoration on Sat 12 Sep. In recent years, some elements have degraded, posing a risk to the arch itself and to the safety of the public who pass beneath To carry out repairs, materials and artisans from China will be sourced so that every facet of its restoration remains true to the culture which it honours. This is part of a wider regeneration of the Chinatown area as the Council works to invest more into the amenity and upkeep Councillor Mandie Shilton Godwin, Executive Member for Clean Air, Environment and Transport, said: “For generations this arch has been a focal point for the Chinese community in Manchester. Ensuring that it remains standing proudly for years to come is a priority for us as a Coun “We know the significance this area holds for many of our residents and that’s why we are committing to further investment, ensuring that it’s not only a top destination for tourists visiting Manchester, but a community that local people feel proud to live and work in

It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and t
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Bolton Car Boot Sale is one of the North West's biggest weekly boot sales, held in the hardstanding car park of the Macron Stadium (formerly Reebok), Burnden Way, Horwich, Bolton BL6 6JW. It runs every Sunday from February right through to December, drawing over 300 sellers and thousands of bargain hunters each week. Sellers can arrive and set up from 6:00 AM, with buyers welcomed in from 7:00 AM. Entry costs just £1 per car for buyers. Pitches for sellers are £14 for a car, £20 for a van and £3 for a trailer, with regular and corner pitches available on request. Bring exact change to keep the queue moving, and call organiser Andrew on 07470784644 for more details. Expect hundreds of stalls across the concrete hardstanding pitches, so it goes ahead in most weather. On-site you'll find a 5-star catering service, doughnuts and coffee, ice cream and desserts, a meat auction, fresh fruit and veg, plants, and retro sweet stalls. The sale is dog-friendly, has male and female toilets, ample parking, and kids' rides and bouncy castles to keep little ones entertained. evidence_packet.summary: Man Utd have conceded twice in every Premier League game this season, and that defensive record could be put to the test this weekend
evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Matthijs de Ligt Manchester United's forgotten man could fix their biggest problem Man Utd have conceded twice in every Premier League game this season, and that defensive record could be put to the test this weekend. Comments Sport Tyrone Marshall Senior Mancheste It was a welcome clean sheet for Manchester United against Sabah on Thursday night, but it's fair to say Manchester City's front line will pose a bigger threat than the journeymen of Azerbaijan this weekend United had conceded twice in their first three Premier League games of the season, but despite a first-half scare, they kept Sabah at arm's length to record a 4-0 win to open their Champions League campaign That soft underbelly could be back in the spotlight on Sunday, however, when Erling Haaland and co rock up at Old Trafford . evidence_packet.evidence_text: Football Manchester United FC Manchester United line-up vs Man City predicted as Rashford returns and Cunha decision made Man United head coach Michael Carrick is hoping to go two for two against Manchester City in the derby this afternoon. Comments Sport opinion Jack Flint Manchester United head into today's game in good spirits after thrashing Sabah FK 4-0 in the Champions League on Thursday night. While there was a clear gulf in quality, Michael Carrick will have been pleased with the ruthlessness of his side. That performance has led to some pos Senne Lammens' spot in goal is secure. He wasn't properly tested on Thursday, but a clean sheet will always be welcomed.
